# dsh-prompt-enhance
**A ✨ button in the DeepSeek Harness composer that rewrites your rough draft into a clear, well-stru
ctured prompt — then puts it straight back into the input box.**
Type a half-formed thought, click once, send a well-specified request. No copy-paste, no second wind
ow, no leaving the conversation.
> Same idea as the "enhance prompt" button in WorkBuddy and similar chat clients, built as a native
as the "enhance prompt" button in WorkBuddy and similar chat clients, built as a native DSH plugin.

## What it looks like
A sparkle button appears in the composer toolbar — **boxed in red above**, between the permission se
lector and the model picker.
It registers into `conversation.input.right`, a **list** slot immediately left of the model selector
. Being a list slot matters: it can coexist with other composer buttons, and it never competes with
the voice-input button that owns the neighbouring single-valued `conversation.input.activity` slot.
### Button states
| State | Look | Meaning |

| Idle | Grey ✨ at 75% opacity, brightens on hover | Ready |
| Busy | Small spinning ring | Waiting

on the model |
| Error | ✨ turns red; hover shows the reason | See Troubleshooting |
| Disabled | 45
% opacity, no hover response | No session, or a submission is in flight |

The rewrite keeps your intent and language, fixes garbled text, makes the goal explicit, and adds st
ructure **only when it helps**. It never invents requirements you did not imply, and it never answer
s the prompt — it only rewrites it.
## Why not just retype it
Retyping works. This exists for the cases where it doesn't:
- **You're thinking out loud.** Voice input, dictation, or a half-finished sentence produces a draft

that is right in substance and wrong in form.
- **You're on the wrong keyboard.** Switching input m

ethods mid-thought breaks flow.
- **You don't know what the agent needs.** A good prompt states the
goal, the subject, the constraint, and what "done" looks like. Knowing that helps; writing it every

time doesn't.
- **Rewrites are cheap and reversible.** The result lands in the draft, not in the sen
d buffer. Edit it, undo it, or ignore it.
## Requirements
| Requirement | Notes |
| **DeepSeek Harness** | Desktop app or a web profile. Built against the bundled bundles; no source

checkout needed. |
| **A working model route** | The plugin calls `ctx.llm.stream()` on an explicitl

y configured provider/model. Whatever you already chat with will do. |
| **`dsh-client-ui-conversati

on`** | Ships with DSH; declared as the client dependency. |
| **`dsh-commands`** | Ships with DSH;
the plugin needs the `commands` service. |
Nothing else. No build step, no dependencies, no npm packages of its own — the plugin is three sourc
else. No build step, no dependencies, no npm packages of its own — the plugin is three source files.

## Configuration
All configuration lives in the profile patch from step 3.
| Field | Type | Required | Meaning |

| `provider` | string | **yes** | Provider route id, e.g. `moxing`, `deepseek-official` |
| `model`
| string | **yes** | Model id on that route, e.g. `deepseek-flash-1017` |
Both must be set together. `ctx.llm.listProviders()` reports provider ids but not their models, and
the session's own resolved route is not exposed to plugin code — so this pair cannot be auto-detecte
d. See Known limitations.
The rewrite instruction is a constant in `index.js` (`SYSTEM_PROMPT`). Fork and edit it if you want
a different rewriting policy — for example, always produce English, or always emit a bullet list.

The command uses `recordInput: false`, so the draft is **not** written into the session log as a use
r message. Nothing reaches the model's conversation history.
